title: Methylene blue
summary: A synthetic dye (1876) that acts as a mitochondrial electron shuttle, boosting ATP production, oxygen use and blood flow even in healthy people. Hormetic — antioxidant at low doses, pro-oxidative at high doses — with cognitive, liver, anti-inflammatory and estrogen-metabolism benefits. Still used IV in hospitals against metabolic poisons such as carbon monoxide and cyanide.

details.what_it_is: Synthetic dye first created in 1876 and the precursor molecule to hydroxychloroquine/chloroquine; still used IV in hospitals to counteract mitochondrial metabolic poisons such as carbon monoxide and cyanide.
mechanisms: Accepts electrons and transfers them directly to oxygen, creating a shortcut in the electron transport chain that boosts ATP production, oxygen use, and blood flow even in healthy individuals.
Activates SIRT1 (a "longevity gene") and AMPK, enhancing fat burning (CPT-1, PPARα).
Acts as a substitute electron acceptor in low-oxygen conditions, helping the liver break down estrogen; works synergistically with niacinamide (preserves NAD+).
Blocks multiple inflammasomes (NLRP3, NLRC4, AIM2) and reduces pro-inflammatory IL-1β and IL-18.
Hormetic: low doses are antioxidant, high doses are pro-oxidative.

benefits.cognitive_support: Influences dopamine and serotonin systems; shown to improve bipolar disorder and severe depression. Its stabilized form LMTM (hydromethylthionine) slows cognitive decline and brain atrophy in Alzheimer's by inhibiting tau protein aggregation.
benefits.liver_health: Enhances fat burning and reduces fat accumulation and inflammation in fatty liver disease, even in animals on a high-fat diet.
benefits.anti_inflammatory: Improved survival in sepsis (LPS) and Listeria infection models.
other: Promotes youthful skin (reduces ROS, stimulates cell proliferation)
Supports bone health against skeletal aging
Mitigates reperfusion injury after a heart attack if given within minutes

side_effects_and_cautions: Blue discoloration of urine/tongue at doses above 30–50 mg
Serotonin syndrome risk when combined with SSRIs (doses >100 mg)
Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency (risk of hemolytic anemia)
Possible GI discomfort, headaches, increased blood pressure

how_to_use.schedule: One day off per week for long-term use
how_to_use.higher_doses: Above 3–5 mg only needed for life-threatening conditions (CO/cyanide poisoning, resistant UTI)
how_to_use.form: Pharmaceutical-grade only, in solid capsule/tablet form via a compounding pharmacy
avoid: Liquid solutions (degrade within 48–72 h via photodegradation, redox reactions, and contamination)
